topic.title: Numeric Literals
topic.description: How to write numeric values in code

sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let's explore how to write numbers in code like a pro! You'll never look at numbers the same way again.

• How to write different types of numbers (whole, decimal, scientific)
• The secret codes for extra-large or tiny numbers
• Why some numbers need special letters (like F or D)

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you're writing a recipe. Some ingredients need exact amounts (like 2 eggs), while others need precise measurements (like 1.5 cups of flour). Numeric literals are like these recipe measurements - but for code!

Numbers in code come in different flavors:
• **Whole numbers** (like 42) - perfect for counting
• **Decimal numbers** (like 3.14) - for precise measurements
• **Scientific notation** (like 1.5E3) - for really big or tiny numbers

Java treats numbers differently based on how you write them. For example:
- `5` is a whole number (int)
- `5.0` is a decimal number (double)
- `5F` is a float (smaller decimal)
- `5E2` is 500 in scientific notation

sections.title: Code Examples
examples:
int decimal = 54;          // decimal literal
int hex = 0x36;            // hexadecimal (same as 54)
int octal = 066;           // octal (same as 54)
int binary = 0b110110;     // binary (same as 54)

long bigNum = 2147483648L; // long literal with L suffix
double sci = 1.5e3;        // scientific notation (1500.0)
float f = 3.14f;           // float literal with f suffix

sections.title: Key Points
points: An integer literal like 42 is of type int by default
A long literal requires the suffix L: 2147483648L
A floating-point literal like 3.14 is of type double by default
A float literal requires the suffix f: 3.14f

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Numbers in code can be written in many ways - choose the right one for your needs. `double` is your best friend for decimal numbers - it's precise and flexible. Practice writing numbers in different formats (scientific, different bases)

questions.question: Which of the following is a floating-point literal in Java?
questions.explanation: 100.0 is a floating-point (double) literal because it contains a decimal point. 100 is an integer literal, and 100L is a long literal.

questions.question: What type does Java assign to the literal 3.14 by default?
questions.explanation: By default, Java treats floating-point literals like 3.14 as double type. To make it a float, you must add an 'f' suffix: 3.14f.
